I am 56. I never went to school, not one day. I have farmed these 14 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. I learned everything from my mother-in-law and from watching the neighbors. My husband and I do the work. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, which helps us buy inputs, but I still count every yuan because fertilizer and diesel are expensive.

I have 10 mu of good flat land near the well. That land I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone around me. The other 4 mu I split: 2 mu for cotton and 2 mu for chili.

For the wheat: Last autumn I rotary tilled and sowed the improved wheat seed, about 12 kg per mu. I put down compound fertilizer, the kind with 15-15-15 on the bag. I bought 8 big bags for the 10 mu, so that is 40 kg per mu. In spring, when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with urea. I buy 5 bags of urea for the 10 mu, that is 25 kg per mu total. I spread half at green-up and half at jointing. Last year I put less on the east corner and the heads were small. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose yield. I irrigate three times from my well: once when it wakes up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds, once for bugs. If the weather is normal I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For the summer maize: After wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed right into the wheat stubble without ploughing. The tractor man charges less and we are in a hurry before the summer rains end. I put the same 40 kg of compound per mu at planting — 8 bags for the 10 mu. When the maize is knee-high and the bottom leaves turn light, I top-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu, that is 4 bags total. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is dry. Two sprays. I should get about 550 kg per mu.

For cotton: I plant hybrid cotton on 2 mu in April. I rotary till first to make good beds. I put one full 50 kg bag of compound per mu, and later when it flowers I add half a bag of urea per mu. Cotton needs water, so I irrigate three times — seedling, flowering, and when the bolls are fat. I spray three times for aphids and mites. Picking is hard work; I might hire two women from the village for a few days. I hope for 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

For chili: 2 mu of fresh chili, transplanted in May. Rotary till first, then one bag of compound per mu as base. When the flowers open I add half a bag of urea per mu. I water four times because chili gets bitter if it dries out. Three sprays for disease. If the market price is not too low, I can harvest about 2000 kg per mu fresh.

I watch old Zhang and my cousin across the road. If they change something and their fields look green and heavy, I will try it next year. I never try new things the first year — change is risky and I cannot afford a bad crop.
